name: Bihari Khichdi
subtitle: loose moong dal and rice khichdi eaten with ghee, chokha and pickle

ingredients.note: 2 tbsp for the tadka, 2 tbsp spooned over at the table
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
the winter version; skip in summer

prepNotes: Rinse the rice and dal together until the water runs almost clear, then leave them to soak 20 minutes. It makes the khichdi break down properly.
Dry-roast the moong dal in a pan for 2 minutes before rinsing if you want the nuttier Mithila version.
Have the chokha and pickle on the table first; khichdi is served the moment it comes off the heat.

steps.text: Drain the soaked rice and dal well.
Heat 2 tbsp ghee in the pressure cooker and crackle the cumin seeds for 20 seconds until they darken a shade.
Add the asafoetida, broken red chillies and bay leaf and fry 10 seconds. The hing should foam and smell sharp.
Stir in the ginger and green chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cauliflower and peas if using and fry 3 minutes until the florets pick up a little colour.
Tip in the drained rice and dal with the turmeric and fry 2 minutes, stirring, until every grain is coated in ghee.
steps.tip: This short fry stops the khichdi turning gluey.

steps.text: Pour in the water, add salt, close the cooker and cook on high for 3 whistles, then off the heat for 10 minutes.
steps.tip: Do not force the pressure down. The khichdi finishes softening in the residual steam.

steps.text: Open the cooker and stir hard for 30 seconds; it should be loose enough to pour off a spoon. Add hot water a splash at a time if it has set.
steps.tip: Bihari khichdi is deliberately sloppy, not fluffy. Err on the wet side.

steps.text: Serve into bowls and spoon the remaining ghee over each portion at the table, with chokha, papad and pickle alongside.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. It sets solid when cold. Reheat on the stovetop with 100 ml hot water per portion, stirring until it pours again.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
